introHeadline: A formal waterfront address built for the Palm Beach buyer who wants permanence.
introDek: South Flagler House is the estate-minded entry in West Palm Beach's new luxury condo pipeline: architectural pedigree, a South Flagler waterfront setting, and a private-club amenity program designed to feel more like a long-term legacy address than a seasonal landing pad.
brookeTake: South Flagler House is the building for buyers who want the visual language of Palm Beach estates translated into a full-service condominium. The draw is not just size or amenities; it is the combination of Robert A.M. Stern architecture, a quieter South Flagler posture, and a club-style amenity package that feels deliberately more formal than the resort/marina energy farther north.
bestFor: Buyers who want a grand, estate-inspired waterfront address
Palm Beach-oriented buyers who want condo service without losing traditional architectural character
Clients comparing South Flagler prestige against North Flagler resort energy
Buyers who care about architectural pedigree and long-term resale audience
signatureFeatures: Designed by Robert A.M. Stern Architects
Developed by Related Ross
Interiors by Pembrooke & Ives
108 residences including larger homes, penthouses, and guest-suite options
Approximately 50,000 square feet of private club amenities
Lakefront pool, cabanas, spa, hydrotherapy, salon, fitness, dining, and sports simulator lounge
amenityNarrative: The amenity program is best understood as a private club layered into a residential building. Rather than relying on one headline feature, South Flagler House stacks wellness, dining, pool, salon, fitness, and social spaces into a full daily-life ecosystem. For buyers, the question is whether they want that depth of in-house service and formality, or whether a more marina/resort-forward building better fits their rhythm.
residenceNarrative: The residences are positioned for buyers who want scale, traditional luxury cues, and a more permanent sense of home. Larger layouts, penthouse offerings, and guest-suite options make the project especially relevant for buyers who are replacing a Palm Beach house or adding a West Palm Beach residence that can live with similar formality.
locationNarrative: South Flagler is its own lane. It is close to Palm Beach, Worth Avenue, Royal Poinciana Plaza, and the Norton Museum, but it feels more residential and composed than the increasingly active North Flagler and Downtown corridors. That quieter posture is part of the value proposition.
buyerComparisonNotes: Compare South Flagler House against Shorecrest and Edgeworth for the Related Ross waterfront pipeline, against Olara for resort/marina lifestyle, and against Ritz-Carlton Residences for branded-service North Flagler living. South Flagler House is the more formal, estate-inspired option in that set.
projectTeamNarrative: The team is central to the pitch: Related Ross as developer, Robert A.M. Stern Architects for the architecture, and Pembrooke & Ives for interiors. Together, the project leans into architectural permanence and Palm Beach-adjacent estate language rather than a glass-tower resort identity.
sourceNotes: Developer source positions the project as a legacy-style waterfront address inspired by Palm Beach's grand estates.

introHeadline: North Flagler resort living with marina, wellness, and culinary identity built in.
introDek: Olara is the resort-minded answer to West Palm Beach waterfront living: expansive amenities, a private marina, wellness programming, and a Jose Andres culinary partnership wrapped into a North Flagler address along the Intracoastal.
brookeTake: Olara is for the buyer who wants the building to feel alive. This is not the quiet-estate version of West Palm Beach luxury. It is more resort, more marina, more food-and-wellness driven, and more connected to the future of North Flagler as a lifestyle corridor.
bestFor: Buyers who want resort-style waterfront living
Boaters or water-oriented buyers drawn to private marina access
Clients who value wellness, dining, service, and amenity volume
Buyers comparing North Flagler momentum against South Flagler formality
signatureFeatures: North Flagler Drive waterfront location along the Intracoastal
Private marina
More than 80,000 square feet of wellness and leisure amenities
Signature dining associated with Chef Jose Andres
Architecture by Arquitectonica
Interiors by Gabellini Sheppard
Lap and leisure pool, spa, fitness, and resort-style service language
amenityNarrative: Olara's amenity story is broad and lifestyle-driven. The marina, spa, pools, dining, and wellness spaces create a building that functions more like a residential resort than a traditional condominium. For buyers, the appeal is convenience and atmosphere: the feeling that much of the daily lifestyle is already waiting downstairs.
residenceNarrative: The residences are positioned around generous scale, waterfront connection, and refined materials. The project is especially relevant for buyers who want new construction with a strong amenity identity but do not necessarily want the more formal, estate-like character of South Flagler House.
locationNarrative: North Flagler is becoming one of West Palm Beach's most important waterfront corridors. Olara benefits from that momentum while offering a more private waterfront setting than Downtown and a more resort-forward identity than South Flagler.
buyerComparisonNotes: Compare Olara against Ritz-Carlton Residences for branded service, Alba for boutique waterfront living, and South Flagler House for a more formal South Flagler estate-style product. Olara's edge is its resort-marina lifestyle and amenity scale.
projectTeamNarrative: The project team reinforces the resort/residential positioning: Arquitectonica brings recognizable South Florida architectural experience, Gabellini Sheppard shapes the interior language, and the Jose Andres dining connection gives the building a stronger culinary identity than most condo projects.
sourceNotes: Developer source describes a luxury waterfront residential oasis with resort-level service, private marina, and major wellness/leisure amenity program.
Official site previously listed residences from approximately $1.7M and indicated construction rising at full scale; verify current status before publication.

introHeadline: The boutique North Flagler waterfront alternative.
introDek: Alba Palm Beach is a smaller-scale waterfront condominium for buyers who want new construction on the Intracoastal without the mega-tower feel. With only 55 residences, townhome options, and a more residential North Flagler setting, Alba sits in a more intimate lane than many of the larger luxury projects nearby.
brookeTake: Alba is compelling because it is not trying to be everything to everyone. It is boutique, direct-waterfront, and more neighborhood-scaled. For the right buyer, that smaller footprint may matter more than having the longest amenity list in town.
bestFor: Buyers who prefer boutique buildings over large towers
Clients who want direct Intracoastal positioning with a quieter residential feel
Buyers looking for a more intimate North Flagler option
Clients considering townhome-style living within a luxury waterfront project
signatureFeatures: Only 55 total residences
Direct Intracoastal waterfront setting
More than 25,000 square feet of dedicated amenity spaces
Two- and three-bedroom residences plus four-bedroom townhomes
Located at 4714 North Flagler Drive
Boutique scale compared with larger West Palm Beach luxury towers
amenityNarrative: Alba offers a meaningful amenity package, but its strongest differentiator is proportion. The building does not need to compete with the largest resort-style amenity programs to make sense; its appeal is a more personal waterfront environment with enough lifestyle support to feel complete.
residenceNarrative: The residence mix gives Alba a different buyer profile than many towers. The inclusion of larger townhome-style options broadens the appeal for buyers who want new construction and waterfront access but still like the feel of a more grounded home environment.
locationNarrative: Alba's North Flagler location is quieter and more residential than Downtown, while still participating in the same broader corridor transformation. It is best understood as a boutique waterfront option rather than a vertical resort.
buyerComparisonNotes: Compare Alba against Olara for North Flagler waterfront lifestyle at a larger scale, Ritz-Carlton Residences for branded service, and South Flagler House for formal estate-inspired luxury. Alba's advantage is intimacy, direct waterfront setting, and boutique building size.
projectTeamNarrative: The project should be presented through its scale, waterfront siting, and residence mix first. Team details should be expanded only from verified official sources to avoid overstating claims.
sourceNotes: Developer source positions Alba as limited-edition boutique waterfront living with 55 residences and dedicated amenity spaces.
Official site referenced final release timing, closings expected to commence in June 2026, and a limited HOA incentive through May 31, 2026. Verify all timing and incentives before publishing.

introHeadline: Branded waterfront service for buyers who want the Ritz-Carlton residential model in West Palm Beach.
introDek: The Ritz-Carlton Residences West Palm Beach brings a globally understood service brand to the local new-construction condo market, pairing North Flagler waterfront positioning with concierge-level operations, wellness amenities, and residences designed for buyers who want polish without necessarily moving into the largest-format estate product.
brookeTake: The Ritz name matters because buyers understand what it is supposed to signal: service, consistency, and a certain hospitality standard. The question is not whether the brand is impressive. The question is whether the residence size, view line, service model, and North Flagler location match how the buyer actually wants to live.
bestFor: Buyers who value branded residential service
Clients who want waterfront new construction with a globally recognizable name
Buyers comparing manageable residence sizes against larger ultra-luxury formats
Clients who want concierge, valet, wellness, and hospitality-style operations

Reported 144-residence waterfront project

Arquitectonica and Rockwell Group design team reported in public coverage
Floor-to-ceiling windows and spacious balconies reported in public coverage
Pool, wellness/fitness center, spa, valet, and 24-hour concierge service reported in public coverage
amenityNarrative: The amenity story is less about sheer square footage and more about the brand/service promise. Buyers should evaluate how the Ritz-Carlton residential service model is implemented day to day: concierge, valet, wellness, common areas, and the overall sense of hospitality within a private residential building.
residenceNarrative: Public reporting has described residences in a more manageable size range than some of the larger estate-style waterfront products. That may appeal to buyers who want new construction, service, views, and brand credibility without taking on the scale of a very large residence.
locationNarrative: North Flagler gives the project waterfront identity and places it inside one of West Palm Beach's most active development corridors. It should be compared not only by brand, but by view quality, access, building scale, and how the surrounding corridor continues to mature.
buyerComparisonNotes: Compare Ritz-Carlton Residences against Olara for resort/marina energy, Alba for boutique North Flagler waterfront living, and South Flagler House for a more formal estate-inspired product. Ritz is the clearest branded-service comparison point in this group.

brookeTake: Shorecrest may become an important comparison point for buyers tracking the Related Ross waterfront pipeline, but this is exactly where the site should avoid confident-sounding mush. Until the official source language is confirmed, the smartest copy is measured: identify the corridor and developer context, then clearly mark what still needs verification.
